title: Derived external cup products for flat algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $X,Y$ algebraic spaces flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Flatness is tested on etale scheme charts; quasi-compactness means inverse images of quasi-compact spaces are quasi-compact, and quasi-separatedness means the relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Use structure-module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the scalar-valued derived global sections of [def-sfb-space-affine-global-sections]. In $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] put $K_Z=R\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$, for $Z=X,Y,X\times_TY$. The canonical external cup product, defined by pulling back along both projections and applying [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product], is an isomorphism in the derived category
$$\kappa_{X,Y}:K_X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{X\times_TY}.$$
Each $K_Z$ is a commutative algebra object: its relative cup product is associative, unital and compatible with derived tensor symmetry. The map $\kappa_{X,Y}$ is an isomorphism of these commutative algebra objects, where its source carries the signed tensor-product multiplication. Pullback by every $T$-morphism between spaces satisfying these hypotheses preserves these products and units. The isomorphisms $\kappa$ are natural for these pullbacks and compatible with associativity, permutations and the unit factor $T$, for which $K_T=R[0]$. Thus pullback by the first projection corresponds to $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and by the second to $y\mapsto1\otimes y$. For every ring map $R\to B$, the canonical comparison $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K_Z\to R\Gamma(Z_B,\mathcal O_{Z_B})$ is an isomorphism and respects the products, units, pullbacks and external cup isomorphisms, and their identity and composition comparisons. If $Z$ is a scheme, the canonical etale--Zariski quasi-coherent derived equivalence identifies this product with the ordinary Zariski structure-module cup product. No projectivity of the cohomology modules, properness, Noetherianity or flatness of $B$ over $R$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $f:X\to T$, $g:Y\to T$, $W=X\times_TY$ and $p:W\to X$, $q:W\to Y$. The fibre product is an algebraic space. Its projections are base changes, so are flat and quasi-compact. The diagonal of a base change is the base change of the diagonal; applying quasi-compact base-change stability also to the diagonals proves quasi-separatedness. Composition preserves quasi-compactness directly from its inverse-image definition. The diagonal of a composite factors through the pullback of each of the two diagonals, proving the corresponding assertion for quasi-separatedness. The diagonal of any morphism of algebraic spaces is a monomorphism, so its own diagonal is an isomorphism; hence each relative diagonal here is also quasi-separated, which is the form of quasi-separatedness required by the projection-formula node used in step 5. On scheme charts, composite flatness says that the composite of two exact tensor functors is exact. Thus $W\to T$, and after any affine scalar extension all three structure maps, satisfy the required hypotheses. Structure modules are quasi-coherent (on an affine chart they are the associated module of its ring), and the cited derived pullback/tensor result supplies quasi-coherent coefficients for the formulas below.

source.place: Tags 08IN, 08IR: geometric hypotheses and quasi-coherent inputs

proof.text: Use the affine equivalence $a_R:D(R)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$, with inverse $G_T$. Its unit sends $r$ to the actual structural section $r\cdot1$. For $h:Z\to T$, the specified compositor identifies $G_Z$ with $G_T Rh_*$. These identifications also identify tensor and scalar insertion: the pullback tensor comparison on flat-term K-flat representatives is the signed total of $(b\otimes u)\otimes(c\otimes v)\mapsto bc\otimes(u\otimes v)$; for $R\to B$ the same formula identifies $La^*a_R(M)$ with $a_B(B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)$. Both are the canonical comparisons, since the scalar-section and compositor definitions fix these formulas and their universal derived units. Thus calculations on $T$ below give calculations in $D(R)$, and $G_T(\mathcal O_T)=R[0]$ with its actual scalar unit.

source.place: Tag 071Q and scalar representative normalization; derived tensor pullback

proof.text: For every ringed-topos morphism $h$ used here put $P_h=Lh^*$, $R_h=Rh_*$, and let $c_h$ be the cup map in the statement. It is exactly the lax map transferred from the strong monoidal $P_h$: its transpose is $(\varepsilon_h\otimes\varepsilon_h)t_h$. The adjunction-mates theorem gives associativity and both unit diagrams, with unit the adjunct of $P_h\mathbf1\simeq\mathbf1$. Symmetry follows by taking transposes: both sides are $(\varepsilon_L\otimes\varepsilon_K)\,\psi\,t_h$, using naturality of the symmetry and the symmetric tensor comparison. Applied to $\mathcal O_Z\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_Z\simeq\mathcal O_Z$, these identities give the commutative algebra structure on $K_Z$; its unit is the structural scalar insertion. This proves the identities as derived morphisms, before taking any cohomology.

source.place: Tags 0FPL (lemma-cup-product-associative), 0FPM (lemma-cup-product-commutative); the unit is the adjunction mate

proof.text: For a $T$-map $u:Z'\to Z$, pullback $\rho_u:K_Z\to K_{Z'}$ is the map whose transpose on $Z'$ is $Lu^*(\varepsilon_{Z,\mathcal O_Z})$ followed by $Lu^*\mathcal O_Z\simeq\mathcal O_{Z'}$. Here the scalar pullback on $Z'$ is identified with $Lu^*P_Z$. The unit and counit of a monoidal adjunction are monoidal, so this transpose, and therefore $\rho_u$, preserves multiplication and unit. Explicitly the two product transposes are $Lu^*(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)t_Z$, followed by the structure-module multiplication; the unit transposes are the structure-module identity. For $v:Z''\to Z'$ the composite-counit formula identifies the transpose of $\rho_v\rho_u$ with $L(uv)^*\varepsilon_Z$. Thus $\rho_v\rho_u=\rho_{uv}$; the identity case uses the identity adjunction. These are the canonical pullbacks, not an arbitrarily chosen system of algebra maps.

Put $A=Rf_*\mathcal O_X$ and $C=Rg_*\mathcal O_Y$ on $T$. They are quasi-coherent derived objects by flat derived base change's preservation clause. The composite
$$A\otimes^{\mathbf L}C\xrightarrow{\pi_g}Rg_*(Lg^*A)\xrightarrow{Rg_*\beta}Rg_*Rq_*\mathcal O_W\simeq R(W\to T)_*\mathcal O_W$$
is an isomorphism: the first arrow is the qcqs projection formula for $g$, with coefficient $\mathcal O_Y$ (using symmetry to order the factors); the second is flat base change for $f$ along $g$, with coefficient $\mathcal O_X$. To identify the map, transpose under $L(W\to T)^*\dashv R(W\to T)_*$. The projection arrow applies the $g$-counit to the $C$ factor. The base-change mate applies $Lp^*$ to the $f$-counit on the $A$ factor. The composite-counit identity therefore gives exactly
$$Lp^*Lf^*A\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lq^*Lg^*C\xrightarrow{Lp^*\varepsilon_f\otimes Lq^*\varepsilon_g}\mathcal O_W\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_W\simeq\mathcal O_W.$$
By the defining cup transpose this is external cup. Step 2 converts it to the specified $\kappa_{X,Y}$ in $D(R)$, proving its invertibility without any assertion about projectivity of $H^i(K_Z)$.

source.place: Tags 08IN (lemma-cohomology-base-change), 08IR (lemma-compare-base-change), with the explicit two-counit transpose

proof.text:
External cup is $m_W(\rho_p\otimes\rho_q)$. For four inputs its composite with multiplication on $K_W$ is, by associativity and symmetry of step 3,
$$m_W\bigl(m_W(\rho_p\otimes\rho_p)\otimes m_W(\rho_q\otimes\rho_q)\bigr)(1\otimes\psi\otimes1).$$
Step 4 replaces the two inner expressions by $\rho_p m_X$ and $\rho_q m_Y$. This is exactly $\kappa$ following the tensor-product multiplication $(m_X\otimes m_Y)(1\otimes\psi\otimes1)$. The unit equation follows from $\rho_p(1)=\rho_q(1)=1$. The symmetry on homogeneous representative tensors of degrees $b,c$ contributes $(-1)^{bc}$, yielding the stated signed multiplication. Consequently $\kappa$ is an algebra morphism, and since its underlying map is invertible it is an algebra isomorphism: compose its multiplicativity and unit equations with its inverse to obtain the same equations for that inverse.

For $u:X'\to X$, $v:Y'\to Y$, use $p(u\times v)=up'$ and $q(u\times v)=vq'$. Functoriality and multiplicativity of pullback from step 4 give
$$\rho_{u\times v}\kappa_{X,Y}=m_{W'}(\rho_{p'}\rho_u\otimes\rho_{q'}\rho_v)=\kappa_{X',Y'}(\rho_u\otimes\rho_v).$$
Both triple-product composites are $m^{(3)}(\rho_{p_1}\otimes\rho_{p_2}\otimes\rho_{p_3})$ by associativity. Interchanging adjacent factors gives the tensor symmetry by commutativity; adjacent interchanges generate permutations, and the symmetry coherence of step 3 identifies their relations. With a factor $T$, the formula is multiplication by its structural unit, hence the appropriate unitor by step 2. Setting the second input to the unit in $\kappa$ gives $\rho_p$, and setting the first to the unit gives $\rho_q$. After $\kappa^{-1}$ these are precisely the two unit-insertion maps stated in the item.

source.place: Tags 0FPL, 0FPM, 0FPN: assembly from the established algebra and pullback identities

proof.text: For $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$, apply flat derived base change to each structure map $h:Z\to T$ and $E=\mathcal O_Z$. The result is the canonical exchange isomorphism $La^*Rh_*\mathcal O_Z\simeq Rh_{B,*}\mathcal O_{Z_B}$, since derived pullback carries the tensor unit to the tensor unit. Step 2 identifies its scalar realization with the canonical comparison $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K_Z\to K_{Z_B}$. The exchange is the counit mate in the cited theorem, so its identity and successive-base-change formulas give the identity and composition comparisons here. Its hypotheses require flatness of $h$, already checked in step 1, and impose no flatness on $a$ or $B$.

Check compatibility for these specified exchange maps $\beta$, rather than just their invertibility. The defining mate equation is
$$\varepsilon_{h_B}\,Lh_B^*(\beta_E)=L(a')^*(\varepsilon_{h,E})\,\theta,$$
where $\theta:Lh_B^*La^*\simeq L(a')^*Lh^*$. It is the identity obtained by transposing $\beta$. For the cup square, transpose under $Lh_B^*\dashv Rh_{B,*}$ and substitute this equation for $E$ and $F$: either route becomes $(L(a')^*\varepsilon_E\otimes L(a')^*\varepsilon_F)$ after $\theta$ and the tensor comparison. Monoidality of $\theta$ gives equality. For the unit both routes transpose to the tensor-unit identity. Hence exchange respects products and units. For a map $u$ between the spaces, pasting the exchange square with the square defining $\rho_u$ gives the same mate as doing them in reverse order, by mate pasting. Thus it respects pullbacks. Apply the exchange/projection tensor-coherence identity to the projection arrow in step 5 and mate pasting to its base-change arrow; their composite is the external-cup square. This proves compatibility with $\kappa$. Identity and iterated scalar extension remain these same diagrams by the identity and pasting assertions, with no extra choices.

source.place: Tag 0H9A (lemma-base-change-cup-product); explicit tensor of counit-mate equations

proof.text: If $Z$ is a scheme, use $\epsilon_Z^*\dashv R\epsilon_{Z,*}$ and the canonical quasi-coherent equivalence. It identifies derived sections and the structure modules. Its pullback is symmetric strong monoidal by the ringed derived comparison theorem. The equivalence's unit and counit are the canonical adjunction maps, and its compatibility with the structure map is the specified derived pullback/direct-image comparison. The composite-counit formula consequently takes the transpose $(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)t$ defining the Zariski cup map to that defining the etale cup map. Adjunction injectivity proves equality of the products, and the same unit transpose identifies the units. This also applies to both projections, so the external product comparison is the ordinary Zariski one. All uses of projection formula and base change were for unbounded quasi-coherent derived objects; none used properness, Noetherianity, projective cohomology, or a flat scalar extension.
